name: Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition
description: The world's most widely played tabletop roleplaying game, published by Wizards of the Coast. Classes, levels and ability scores, from 1st to 20th. Incudo reads the same community content Aurora Builder did, covering the core books, supplements and Unearthed Arcana.

characterKinds.name: Player Character
characterKinds.description: Levels 1–20, a class, a background, and the two-page sheet everyone means when they say "character".

additions.description: Anything from your content, whatever its prerequisites: one whose prerequisites are not met is added and marked. A spell added here is cast as one of the character's spellcasting classes, which you choose (the only one is chosen for you): that class's save DC, attack bonus and spell slots apply to it, and if the class prepares spells it is always prepared. Cast through no class, none of them apply.

references.label: For reference
references.description: Text from your content to keep beside this character, such as the stat block of a creature your spell summons or a beast you can turn into. It is shown here and on the sheet, and saved with the character. Nothing is worked out from it.

companions.label: Companions
companions.description: Creatures this character has from its features, spells and items, each with its own stat block. Where a creature’s stat block depends on this character, such as a steel defender’s hit points, the numbers here follow this character.

sheet.label: Saving Throws
sheet.description: The saving throws the creature is proficient in. Any other is the ability modifier.

sheet.label: Skills
sheet.description: The skills the creature is proficient in. Any other is the ability modifier.

sheet.label: Defences and Languages
sheet.description: As the creature’s stat block prints them.

sheet.label: Added by Its Holder
sheet.description: What the character's features add to this creature's attack and damage rolls. Its actions print their numbers without it.

elementNote.text: If it is an attack, its holder adds {{companion:attack}} to the attack roll and {{companion:damage}} to the damage.

buildSteps.label: Ability Scores
buildSteps.description: Roll, buy, or take the standard array. First because what you rolled is a real input into which class is worth playing.

buildSteps.label: Campaign options
buildSteps.description: Optional rules a table may use, such as feats or customized ability score increases. A new character starts with feats and multiclassing on, as most tables play; switch off what yours does not use.

buildSteps.label: Optional class features
buildSteps.description: Features your classes may take beside their own, some of them in place of one of their own, offered once you have chosen a class. Each gives its feature from the class level it names, and one that replaces a feature takes that feature away while it is taken. Taking none is the ordinary answer.

buildSteps.label: Additional features
buildSteps.description: Things a table may allow beyond the rules a character is built by: another speed or sense, a feat or multiclass prerequisite waived, weapon mastery, a companion or familiar of your choice, lycanthropy. Take only what your table allows; taking none is the ordinary answer.

buildSteps.label: Ability score adjustments
buildSteps.description: A score raised or lowered by one beyond what the scores and the build give, for a table that grants or imposes one. Taking none is the ordinary answer.

freeform.label: About the character
freeform.description: Text no rule reads: who plays the character, how they look, what drives them, and notes. Whatever is written here is shown on the sheet.

sections.label: Attacks
sections.description: Every weapon the character carries, and an unarmed strike. The attack bonus is the ability modifier (Strength, Dexterity for a ranged weapon, the higher of the two for a finesse one), plus the proficiency bonus for a weapon the character is proficient with, plus a magic weapon's bonus and what features add; the damage adds the same modifier and magic bonus. With a light melee weapon in each hand, the off-hand attack's damage adds no positive ability modifier unless the character has a two-weapon fighting style.

sections.label: Saving Throws
sections.description: The ability modifier, plus the proficiency bonus for a saving throw the character is proficient in (listed under Proficiencies).

sections.label: Skills
sections.description: The ability modifier, plus the proficiency bonus for a skill the character is proficient in (listed under Proficiencies), twice it with expertise.

sections.label: Wild Shape
sections.description: The beasts the character can turn into at its druid level: the highest challenge rating and what the beast may not have. It must also be a beast the character has seen.

sections.label: Spell Slots
sections.description: Shared by the character's spellcasting classes.

characterKinds.name: NPC / Monster
characterKinds.description: A stat block rather than a sheet, with a challenge rating instead of a level. Start from a creature in your content and change any score it prints, or start from nothing and enter the scores yourself. Traits and actions are picked directly.

additions.description: Anything from your content, whatever its prerequisites: one whose prerequisites are not met is added and marked. A spell added here is cast as one of the character's spellcasting classes, which you choose (the only one is chosen for you): that class's save DC, attack bonus and spell slots apply to it, and if the class prepares spells it is always prepared. Cast through no class, none of them apply.

references.label: For reference
references.description: Text from your content to keep beside this creature, such as a stat block printed only as prose. It is shown here and on the sheet, and saved with the creature. Nothing is worked out from it: enter the numbers and features yourself.

buildSteps.label: Creature
buildSteps.description: The creature this one is, if your content has it. Skip it to build one by hand.

buildSteps.label: Ability Scores
buildSteps.description: What the creature prints, or what you enter. A score you enter replaces the printed one.

buildSteps.label: Armor Class, Hit Points and Speed
buildSteps.description: What the creature's stat block gives, or what you enter. A number you enter replaces the creature's.

freeform.label: About the creature
freeform.description: Text no rule reads: how it looks and acts, and the DM's notes. Whatever is written here is shown on the sheet.

sections.label: Saving Throws
sections.description: The saving throws the creature is proficient in. Any other is the ability modifier.

sections.label: Skills
sections.description: The skills the creature is proficient in. Any other is the ability modifier.

sections.label: Defences and Languages
sections.description: As the creature’s stat block prints them.

sections.label: Legendary Actions
sections.description: What the creature gives. Build it as a Legendary Creature to set how many it takes a round, or to add more.

sections.label: Lair Actions and Regional Effects
sections.description: What the creature gives. Build it as a Legendary Creature to add more.

characterKinds.name: Legendary Creature
characterKinds.description: An NPC that also takes legendary actions, and may have lair actions and regional effects. The official content has these only as text in a creature's description, so write them on the creature as features of its own, or add a file of your own content that declares them.

characterKinds.name: Sidekick
characterKinds.description: A creature that gains levels in a sidekick class. Its stat block is where it starts, and each level adds hit points, a proficiency bonus by level and the class's features. Sidekick classes are not part of the game's open rules, so they come from content you add yourself, such as a content file of your own.

available.note: A sidekick needs a sidekick class, and no loaded source has one. Add a content source or file that has sidekick classes.

buildSteps.label: Creature
buildSteps.description: The creature that becomes the sidekick. Its stat block is where the sidekick starts: its scores, armor class, hit points and hit die.
